name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Vigil ADS-22 'Nightwatch'
description:
A precision rifle optimized for nocturnal and low-visibility engagement, integrating a cryogenically-cooled infrared sensor array that provides the operator with thermal imaging resolution sufficient to identify facial features at 1,500 meters in total darkness. The ADS-22 fires tracer-less conventional rounds to avoid revealing the shooter's position.

Arcturus designed the Nightwatch for corporate perimeter defense during GLMZ's artificial night cycles, when thermal contrast between human bodies and urban infrastructure reaches maximum. The weapon's sensor suite can distinguish between human body signatures, synthetic mimics, and thermal decoys — a capability developed after several incidents where corporate snipers wasted ammunition on drone-deployed heat sources.

The Vigil's BCI integration projects the thermal image directly into the operator's visual cortex, allowing them to maintain situational awareness without looking through an eyepiece. Operators describe the experience as seeing heat itself — a world rendered in temperature rather than light.
legality: Licensed — corporate security and military night operations
specifications:
caliber: 7.62mm tracer-less match-grade
effective_range: 100-1,800 meters
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic, 1 round per 2 seconds
capacity: 10-round detachable magazine
weight: 7.4 kg
power_source: Sensor suite: cryo-cell, 6 hours continuous imaging
tactical_use: The Nightwatch dominates low-visibility engagements. While other precision weapons rely on ambient light amplification or laser illumination — both of which can be detected — the ADS-22's passive thermal system leaves no electromagnetic footprint. The shooter sees everything and reveals nothing. Corporate perimeter teams deploy Nightwatch operators during night cycles as the primary detection and engagement layer, trusting the thermal discrimination AI to filter genuine threats from environmental noise.
cultural_context: Arcturus's night operations equipment has earned the company a reputation as the manufacturer of darkness. The Nightwatch embodies this identity — a weapon that turns the absence of light into an advantage. In GLMZ's lower tiers, where artificial lighting is unreliable, the knowledge that Nightwatch operators might be watching creates a curfew more effective than any official mandate.
story_hooks: A Nightwatch operator reported seeing thermal signatures in a supposedly abandoned section of the lower tiers — hundreds of heat sources, all stationary, all at exactly the same temperature. When a reconnaissance team investigated, the section was empty. The thermal ghosts remain unexplained.
Someone has developed a personal thermal masking system that defeats the ADS-22's discrimination AI. Arcturus is offering a bounty for a working sample.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purpose-built sniper rifle with a distinctly modular aesthetic. The Nightwatch presents as a narrow, almost skeletal frame compared to conventional rifles — its thermal sensor array dominates the upper receiver, creating an asymmetrical silhouette where sensitive optics take visual precedence over barrel profile. The overall impression is surgical precision married to cold efficiency.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 118 cm | Barrel length: 66 cm | Sensor array housing: 28 cm | Width at receiver: 8 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively balanced at 7.4 kg — the weight sits forward in the sensor assembly and cryo-cell housing, creating a counterweight that reduces perceived muzzle heaviness. Feels assured in trained hands; the engineering speaks of deliberate load distribution.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum alloy chassis with carbon-composite furniture. The sensor array housing is a proprietary polymer-ceramic composite designed for thermal stability and vibration damping. Cryo-cell casing is reinforced steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with selective brushed aluminum accents around the sensor array. The finish is deliberately non-reflective — no shine, no glint. Areas around the cryo-cell show subtle frost patterns even at rest, a faint reminder of the cryogenic temperatures within.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary | Brushed aluminum accents | Deep charcoal furniture | Faint azure indicator lights (dormant until powered)
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with subtle contouring — textured enough for gloved operation in cold conditions, but not aggressive. The grip subtly angles inward, designed for BCI-integrated operators who maintain looser hand contact since aiming is handled via neural interface.
distinctive_features: Prominent cryogenic sensor array mounted above the receiver — a rectangular housing with visible cooling fins
Dual cryo-cell batteries mounted on either side of the receiver in recessed housings, showing faint frost accumulation
Thermal targeting reticle etched into the rail system (non-functional without BCI activation)
Minimal iron sights — the Nightwatch assumes BCI integration, making traditional backup sights unnecessary
Heat dissipation vents along the barrel shroud, barely visible as subtle grooming in the composite material
Small azure LED indicators clustered near the magazine well (dormant in standby)
Magazine well features thermal-signature discrimination markings
Modular quick-disconnect points at three locations, suggesting field-replaceable subsystems
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: The Arcturus Defense Solutions logo — a stylized 'ADS' in serif font — is engraved (not printed) on the left side of the receiver. Below it, in smaller characters: 'VIGIL ADS-22 NIGHTWATCH | THERMAL DESIGNATION SYSTEM | SN: [Individual]'. A third marking reads 'CRYO-CELL: 6H CONTINUOUS | LICENSED CORPORATE USE ONLY' in red anodized text, a legal compliance statement. Serial plate is located on the underside of the receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field examples show minimal wear — the matte finish hides dust better than traditional finishes, and the robust engineering produces few cosmetic tells of hard use. Cryo-cell housings show occasional condensation rings. Operators report that Nightwatch rifles age gracefully; a five-year-old unit looks functionally identical to a new one. Battle damage is rare (operators don't survive close-quarters engagement with a 1,500-meter precision rifle) but, when present, manifests as clean strikes to the chassis rather than the sensor array — the sensitive components are guarded by their protective housing.
